expected_observation: Standalone primary may move modestly, but within-user rank correlation with the parent should drop on tab-sensitive slices and portfolio marginal contribution should improve if the residual branch corrects those slices.

experiment_contract.claim: Test whether a tab-specialized residual scorer fused with the base LambdaRank score improves tab-slice ordering and portfolio complementarity.
experiment_contract.expected_observable: Prediction hashes differ from the parent, and tab-conditioned score distributions show non-constant adjustments varying by both tab and item context.
experiment_contract.falsification_condition: Trusted validation shows no gain in primary or no evidence of complementary contribution; or implementation degenerates to a per-user/per-tab constant shift only.
forbidden_shortcuts: using any post-exposure feedback as inference features
changing only a scalar post-hoc tab bias per row without training the residual head
claiming fusion while reusing only one parent mechanism
required_components: features block appends explicit tab/duration interaction columns
train block fits both base SO.train model and a separate residual head on the new columns
predict block combines the two branch outputs with a fixed predeclared weight

fallback: If harmful, keep the tab-interaction features idea but drop the extra branch and test them as pure tree inputs in a later isolated architecture experiment.
hypothesis: A small tab/context residual branch will correct systematic ordering errors where the current tree leaf is weak, especially on tabs 0/2/4/6, producing complementary within-user reordering and better marginal portfolio contribution.
implementation_plan: Edit features, train, and predict. In features, append a small set of legal interaction columns that expose tab-specific behavior without labels: one-hot flags for major tabs seen in diagnostics (0,1,2,4,6), duration_ms transforms such as log1p(duration_ms), and tab×log_duration interactions, while retaining all base SO.build_features columns. In train, fit the base SO.train LambdaRank model as-is on the augmented matrix, then also fit a lightweight sklearn logistic regression residual head on train rows using only the new interaction columns to predict long_view; standardize only inside train if needed. In predict, output base rank score plus a small fixed-weight residual adjustment from the residual head. This is a bounded two-branch fusion inside one candidate.
justification: Because portfolio search is active and convergence is high, a structural error-diversifying branch targeted at a diagnosed weakness is preferable to scalar retuning. Using only inference-time tab and duration interactions respects leakage rules and creates a candidate whose errors need not be highly correlated with the current tree leaf.
mechanism: tab-specialized residual blend over base lambdarank
observation: Portfolio diagnostics show strong tab specialization mismatch: w003 has member disadvantages on tab=0 (-0.01749022029153391) and tab=2 (-0.009346696620826433), while w001 and w002 are stronger on some tab slices; the last measured candidate also regressed on every reported tab slice, including tab 2 (-0.004738620736890686), tab 4 (-0.005241128435804598), and tab 6 (-0.004047385767926126).
research_nonuse_reason: No supplied research record directly describes this tab-residual fusion for the current parent. The strongest basis is the trusted tab-slice diagnostics plus the active portfolio directive requiring an error-diverse or structural idea.
risk: Residual logistic branch may optimize pointwise probability rather than ranking and could hurt base ordering
Added interactions may be redundant with tree splits and provide little diversity
Score-scale mismatch could overpower the base model if blend weight is too large
